חָזַר
1) to go around (searching). Kohelet Rabbah to VII, 8 הוא חוֹזֵר עליה he searches it again (tries to recover his scholarship); ib. יכול הוא לַחֲזוֹר עליה he may recover it; and e.; see infra.

—2) to turn around, return; to retract, repent. Ib. חֲזוֹר בך come back (repent)! Eduy. V, 6 חזור בך withdraw thy opposition.—Demai IV, 1 חָזְרָה למקומה came back to its place (was mixed up again). Ma'aser Sheni I, 5 יֶחְזְרוּ דמים וכ׳ the money shall return to its former condition, i.e. the sale is annulled, and the money has again its sacred character. Keritot 8ᵃ נַחֲזוֹר על הראשונות let us go back to what was said first. Shabbat 118ᵇ; Arakhin 15ᵇ מימי … וחָזַרְתִּי לאחורי I never said a word (about a fellowman) on which I went back (when confronted with him). Kiddushin 59ᵃ וחָזְרָה בה and she reconsiders (her consent to be married); חוֹזֶרֶת she may do so; Gittin 32ᵇ. Ib. חוזר ומגרש בו dare he use the same letter of divorce again (after he has revoked it)? Terumot IV, 3 ח׳ והוסיף then again he added. Gittin IV, 5 חָזְרוּ לומר then again they said (added); and see from

Piël - חִיזֵּר to go around from one to the other. Yevamot 53ᵃ צריכה לְחַזֵּר על וכ׳ she must apply to all the brothers successively; (ib. 26ᵇ; 51ᵇ לַחֲזוֹר). Yerushalmi Taanit IV, 68ᵃ bottom of page חִיזַּרְנוּ על כל וכ׳ we searched the whole Bible; Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. I, beginning 39ᵃ חי׳ בכל וכ׳; (Sifré Devarim section (Parashah) 1 חָזַרְנוּ). Yerushalmi Bava Batra VIII, 16ᶜ top, see דיאתימון. Kiddushin 2ᵇ לחַזֵּר על אשה to go around in search of a wife (to woo). Ib. מי חוֹזֵר על מי (Kal) which of them goes around &c.?; Niddah 31ᵇ מי מְחַזֵּר וכ׳.

Hifil - הֶחֱזִיר
1) to restore, give back. Berakhot 27ᵇ המַחֲזִיר שלים לרבו he who returns the plain salutation (shalom) of his teacher (without adding, ‘My teacher’). Ib. 32ᵇ לא ה׳ לו שלום did not answer his greeting. Bava Metzia 7ᵇ יַחֲזִיר לאשה he must restore (the lost document) to the wife. Ketubot 73ᵇ והֶחֱזִירָהּ and re-married her; and from

—2) to revoke; to reconsider, to grant a new trial. Gittin VI, 3 אם רצה להַחֲזִיר לא יַחֲזִיר if the husband wants to revoke the letter of divorce, he cannot do so.—Sanhedrin IV, 1 דיני נפשות מַחֲזִירִין וכ׳ in capital cases verdicts may be reconsidered in favor of the defendant. Ib. VI, 1 מחזירין the convict is brought back for a new trial; and from—[Ib. 33ᵇ חוזר, אין מחזירין Manuscript Florence (ed. חוזרין).]—Eduy. V, 7 החזרת בך, Mishnah ed. חָזַרְתָּ, see supra.

—3) to make one read over, to cause correction. Yerushalmi Megillah IV, 74ᵈ מחזירין אותו we order him to read it over again correctly. Berakhot 29ᵃ; and from

עִילָה, עִילָא f. (עָלַל; compare בִּילָה from בָּלַל) [going about, bringing about; compare סִיבָּה end,]
1) circumstance, cause; pretext. Ketubot 20ᵇ ע׳ מצאו וטהרו וכ׳ they found some (paltry) reason to declare clean a spot in the land of Israel; Nazir 65ᵇ עילא; [Rashi: עילא = עילעא rib of a human body]. Yerushalmi Ketubot III, end, 28ᵃ מצאתי ע׳ לשחררו I have found an opportunity to set him free. Yerushalmi Terumot X, 47ᵇ; Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. II, 42ᵃ (in Chald. dict.) על ידי ע׳, see זְבִינְתָּא. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 20; section (Parashah) 45; section (Parashah) 63 ואף היא על ידי ע׳ and even this in a round-about way (indirectly); and e.

—2) crookedness, insidiousness, falsehood. Eduy. V, 7 שמא ע׳ מצאת בי (Mishnah ed. עַוְלָה; Manuscript Munich עָוֶל) hast thou found any falsehood in me? Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 28 נפלו עליהם בע׳ they turned against them with insidiousness.—V. עֲלִילָה.

רָחַק (Biblical Hebrew) to be distant, far, removed. Y’lamdenu (a lost book, corresponding to Tanḥuma, quoted in Arukh) to Bamidbar X, 29, quot. in Arukh (reference. to Psalms LXXIII, 27) מי שרוֹחֵק הק"בה וכ׳ (ed. Kohelet שׁמִתְרַחֵק) he who keeps away from the Lord, so as not to repent. Sifré Bamidbar 131 כרְחוֹק מזרח וכ׳ as far as the east is removed from the west; and e.

Piël - רִחֵק, רִיחֵק to remove; to alienate; to reject, expel; to loathe. Bava Kamma 24ᵃ top, and e. ר׳ נגיחותיו if the ox did his gorings in intervals (of three days), opposed קירב. Ib. רִיחֲקָה ראיותיה, see רְאִיָּה. Yalkut Psalms 809 (reference. to Psalms l. common gender.) זה … שׁרִחֲקוּ את הקץ this alludes to Balaam and his associates, who put far off the end (the day of judgment, Bamidbar XXIV, 17), opposed קרבו. Berakhot 60ᵇ ורַחֲקֵנִי מאדם רע וכ׳ keep me far from a bad man and a bad associate. Eduy. V, 7 מעשיך יקרבוך ומעשיך יְרַחֲקוּךָ thy own doings will bring thee near (win thee friends), and thy own doings will alienate thee. Ib. VIII, 7 לרַחֵק, see קָרֵב; and from—Part. pass. מְרוּחָק; plural מְרוּחָקִים, מְרוּחָקִין. Ib. המר׳ בזרוע, see קָרֵב. Berakhot 63ᵇ שלא היה מר׳ וכ׳ which was only twelve miles off.

Hifil - הִרְחִיק same. Sifré Bamidbar 94 מַרְחִיקִים, see קָרֵב. Bava Batra II, 5 מַרְחִיקִין את הסולם וכ׳ (neighbors) must keep a ladder removed from the (neighbor’s) dove-cote four cubits. Ib. 4 אלא אם כן ה׳ ממנו וכ׳ unless he places (the wall) at a distance of four cubits. Ib. 18ᵇ על המזיק להַרְחִיק את עצמו it is the duty of him who causes the damage to remove himself; (oth. opinion) על הניזק להרחיק וכ׳ he who is injured must remove himself. Berakhot I, 1 כדי להרחיק וכ׳ in order to keep men away (prevent them) from sin. Sanhedrin 103ᵇ שהִרְחִיקָה וכ׳, see לְגִימָה. Ib. מַרְחֶקֶת וכ׳
estranges those who are near (related) &c.; and from—2) to keep aloof, stay away. Pirkei Avot I, 7 הַרְחֵק משכן רע keep aloof from a bad neighbor; and e.—[Y. Berakhot I, 2ᵈ bottom of page והרחיק על פתחו וכ׳, read: והִרְתִּיק, see רָתַק.]

Hithpaël - הִתְרַחֵק,

Nithpaël - נִתְרַחֵק to remove one’s self; to become a stranger. Yevamot 109ᵃ לעולם ידבק … ויִתְרַחֵק וכ׳ man should always cling to three things, and keep aloof from three things. Sanhedrin III, 4 קרוב ונ׳, see קָרוֹב. Berakhot 34ᵇ (reference. to Isaiah LVII, 19) שהיה קרוב … ונ׳ וכ׳ who came near committing a sin, and withdrew himself from it. Y’lamdenu (a lost book, corresponding to Tanḥuma, quoted in Arukh) l. common gender., see supra; and e.

שְׁמוּעָה f. (Biblical Hebrew; שָׁמַע)
1) report, news. Rosh Hashanah 3ᵃ (reference. to Bamidbar XXI, 1) מה ש׳ שמע וכ׳ what was the report he heard? He heard that Aaron was dead. Ib. 18ᵇ שבו באת ש׳ וכ׳ on it (the fifth of Tebeth) came the report to the captivity that the city was taken (Ezekiel XXXIII, 21); עשו יום ש׳ וכ׳ they observed mourning on the day they heard the news, as they would have done on the day when the Temple was burnt. Ketubot 62ᵃ ש׳ דבית המקדש the news of the destruction of the Temple. Moʿed Katan 20ᵇ, and from ש׳ רחוקה the news of the death of a relative received after thirty days from the time of death; ש׳ קרובה news received within thirty days. Sanhedrin 110ᵃ; and from—plural שְׁמוּעוֹת. Berakhot IX, 2, see בְּשׂוֹרָה. Moʿed Katan 26ᵃ ש׳ הרעות bad news; and see from

—2) tradition, traditional decision, legal discussion (הֲלָכָה). Ib. 23ᵃ אין אומרים ש׳ והגדה וכ׳ you must not speak of legal subjects or homiletical interpretations in the house of mourning. Sanhedrin 88ᵃ הוא אומר מפי הש׳ if he says, I gave my decision on the basis of a tradition, opposed כך הוא בעיני it is my own opinion. Eduy. V, 7 אני עמדתי בשְׁמוּעָתִי … בשְׁמוּעָתָן I stood by my tradition, and they by theirs. Eruvin 64ᵃ כל האומר ש׳ זו וכ׳ he who says, this traditional decision is good, the other is not &c. Menachot 18ᵃ כמדומה אני שלא כיווננו שְׁמוּעָתֵינוּ וכ׳ it seems to me that until now our traditions did not correspond; Tosefta Zevachim II, 17 שמועתן (correct accordingly); and from—plural as ab. Chagigah 14ᵃ גבור בעל ש׳ ‘a mighty man’ (Isaiah III, 2) that means a man knowing many legal traditions.—[שְׁמוּעָה in Chald. dict., see next word]

comments.en: You shall neither side with the mighty to do wrong—you shall not give perverse testimony in a dispute so as to pervert it in favor of the mighty—
comments.he: לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרֵֽי־רַבִּ֖ים לְרָעֹ֑ת וְלֹא־תַעֲנֶ֣ה עַל־רִ֗ב לִנְטֹ֛ת אַחֲרֵ֥י רַבִּ֖ים לְהַטֹּֽת׃

sections.en: At the time of his death he said to his son, “Retract the four opinions which I used to declare.” He (the said to him, “Why did not you retract them?” He said to him, “I heard them from the mouth of the many, and they heard [the contrary] from the mouth of the many. I stood fast by the tradition which I heard, and they stood fast by the tradition which they heard. But you have heard [my tradition] from the mouth of a single individual and [their tradition] from the mouth of the many. It is better to leave the opinion of the single individual and to hold by the opinion of the many.” He said to him, “Father commend me to your colleagues.” He said to him, “I will not commend you.” He said to him, “Have you found in me any wrong?” He said, “No; your own deeds will cause you to be near, and your own deeds will cause you to be far.”
sections.he: בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָתוֹ אָמַר לִבְנוֹ, בְּנִי, חֲזֹר בְּךָ בְאַרְבָּעָה דְבָרִים שֶׁהָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר. אָמַר לוֹ, וְלָמָּה לֹא חָזַרְתָּ בָּךְ. אָמַר לוֹ, אֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי מִפִּי הַמְרֻבִּים, וְהֵם שָׁמְעוּ מִפִּי הַמְרֻבִּים. אֲנִי עָמַדְתִּי בִשְׁמוּעָתִי, וְהֵם עָמְדוּ בִשְׁמוּעָתָן. אֲבָל אַתָּה שָׁמַעְתָּ מִפִּי הַיָּחִיד, וּמִפִּי הַמְרֻבִּין. מוּטָב לְהַנִּיחַ דִּבְרֵי הַיָּחִיד, וְלֶאֱחֹז בְּדִבְרֵי הַמְרֻבִּין. אָמַר לוֹ, אַבָּא, פְּקֹד עָלַי לַחֲבֵרֶיךָ. אָמַר לוֹ, אֵינִי מַפְקִיד. אָמַר לוֹ, שֶׁמָּא עִילָה מָצָאתָ בִי. אָמַר לוֹ, לָאו. מַעֲשֶׂיךָ יְקָרְבוּךָ וּמַעֲשֶׂיךָ יְרַחֲקוּךָ:
